reviews.title: Woah brochacho
reviews.text:
As a Colorado endurance brochacho, I downloaded the Wahoo app expecting clean ride data, not a full-on data privacy nightmare. The app seems way too interested in collecting and connecting everything short of my favorite burrito spot, and the privacy controls don’t exactly inspire confidence.

Trying to delete my account was like signing up for Comcast customer service: endless menus, mysterious hoops, and the creeping suspicion that my request had been shipped off to a magical farm where deleted accounts go to live forever. I kept waiting for someone to tell me, “You can’t cancel—your account is part of the system now.”

The fitness features are solid, but I’d rather track my intervals than negotiate with a corporate bureaucracy from a certain Colorado mountain town. Wahoo, please make privacy clearer and account deletion a straightforward button—not an epic quest through increasingly absurd support channels.

reviews.title: Close in Being Perfect for V3 GPS units
reviews.text:
Update: App did now add quick access to load routes and workouts on GPS units but still doesn’t allow sharing live link easily which are most frequently used actions by users. 90% there!

reviews.title: Frustratingly Inconsistent App
reviews.text:
I originally started using the Wahoo app to record my indoor cycling rides and upload my power and cadence data to Strava using my Favero Assioma power pedals paired to the app. 

On my first few rides, I actually found the app insightful and promising enough that I decided to try the paid version.

Unfortunately, I quickly realized the app was far too unreliable to justify paying for it. Even with recorded rides, it was basically a 50/50 chance whether the workout would successfully upload within the app itself. 

Because of the constant glitches, I canceled the subscription and went back to the free version.

The free version is so frustrating on the basic end. Many rides simply fail to upload to Strava. Even when attempting manual uploads, they often fail repeatedly despite multiple retries, restarting my phone, signing out and back in, and other troubleshooting steps. At a certain point, the app becomes exhausting to deal with.

What makes this especially frustrating is that when you finish a hard ride expecting the app to do the one thing it is supposed to do, which is reliably record and sync your workout data, and instead you end up with nothing to show for it.

I know this issue is specifically related to Wahoo because my Apple Watch heart rate data uploads to Strava without issue, and I tested another cycling app that recorded and synced my rides successfully using the same equipment.

I ultimately deleted the Wahoo app and switched to an app called “Cadence” instead. 

I had even considered investing in Wahoo smart bikes or bike trainers at one point, but after this experience, I simply cannot trust the reliability of their software ecosystem when even the basic ride recording and syncing experience is this inconsistent.

Very disappointing experience overall.

Very bad stewardship

reviews.title: Sad degradation of functionality with the inclusion of many  features
reviews.text:
Compared to the previous app to control element devices this one is severely crippled, consistent failures to send routes or way points for auto route creation. Constant lack of communication with the phone and erroneous syncing issues. There’s still no way to turn off the computer and resume it without the auto cancel ride feature being activated (Bolt). These apps and computers have just been a slow slide of developers not listening to the users and going ahead with whatever they see as interesting or profitable. Example: The new app pushes a bunch of AI features and auto coaching things in your face without having the basic core functionality of the previous app.

Sad. But there’s no better options from garmin or hammerhead so I feel stuck here.
